# Research Report: Does Ibuprofen Worsen COVID-19?

## Conclusion
The claim that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 infection is **not supported by current evidence**. The concern originated from theoretical mechanisms and anecdotal reports, but subsequent studies and reviews have failed to demonstrate a causal link between ibuprofen use and worse COVID-19 outcomes.

## Origin of the Claim
The alarm began in March 2020 when French health authorities suggested anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen could exacerbate COVID-19. This was partly based on a letter by Fang et al. arguing that ibuprofen increases ACE-2 activity, potentially enhancing coronavirus infection ([PMC7151542](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7151542/); [UCLA Health](https://www.uclahealth.org/news/article/can-ibuprofen-worsen-covid-19-an-expert-offers-the-truth)). The WHO initially supported this claim but then reversed course, stating there was no evidence that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 ([CBC News](https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ibuprofen-covid-19-novel-coronavirus-1.5501496)).

## Evidence Against the Claim
- A **nationwide study** found "no significant association between recent ibuprofen prescription claims and the composite end point" of severe COVID-19 ([PMC7537121](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7537121/)).
- Multiple reviews concluded that "current epidemiologic evidence is not strong enough to infer a causal link of a harmful effect of ibuprofen in patients with COVID-19" ([PMC7151542](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7151542/)).
- A **38-site observational study** noted that while early anecdotal reports suggested increased risk, "subsequent observational studies failed to demonstrate increased risk and in one case showed reduced risk associated with NSAID use" ([PMC9107579](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9107579/)).

## Summary
The initial concern was based on mechanistic speculation and anecdotal reports, not robust clinical data. Subsequent research has not supported the claim, and major health organizations including the WHO have clarified that there is no evidence ibuprofen worsens COVID-19.
